title: Debt and Cover
premise: Xanthe Amberdale, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office — an embassy that exists on no map and no ledger — is handed a burner phone recovered from a dead courier. When it rings, the voice belongs to her mentor, Elias Vane, who officially died two years ago. Following the calls, Xanthe uncovers a plot to destroy a bridge during the Aldermoor Summit, staged as structural failure so no nation claims responsibility. As she works the case off the books, she discovers the Meridian Office itself sanctioned the attack to force a security pact, and Vane is alive inside the conspiracy, testing whether she will choose loyalty or truth. In the end, Xanthe stops the bombing, exposes the order through a dead-drop archive rather than the courts, burns her own cover to do it, and walks away from the Office with Vane's fate — and her conscience — unresolved.
about_author: Lena Eastwick spent eleven years in logistics for humanitarian missions before turning to fiction, a career that taught her how institutions bury inconvenient truths. She writes from a coastal town whose name she declines to confirm.

chapters.title: The Phone That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She closes a routine deniability job — erasing a diplomat's affair from three databases — when a courier dies at her feet outside a Lisbon tram stop, leaving a burner phone in her coat pocket. The beat: professional detachment cracking into unease as she realizes someone chose her deliberately.

chapters.title: Meridian Rules
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the Office's unmarked chancery, her handler Corvus orders her to surrender the phone; she reports it destroyed but keeps it. Flashback texture establishes her debt to the institution that recruited her out of a war-crimes tribunal scandal. Beat: loyalty asserted, quietly tested.

chapters.title: A Voice Two Years Dead
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The phone rings at 3 a.m.; the voice is Elias Vane, her mentor, officially killed in a Prague car bomb. He gives her one sentence — 'Count the maintenance crews at the Aldermoor crossing' — and hangs up. Beat: grief weaponized into obsession.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, with an intercut of an anonymous saboteur's POV. She surveils the Verre Bridge, the summit convoy route, and finds an inspection crew whose credentials dissolve under scrutiny. The intercut shows epoxy being poured into a load-bearing joint. Beat: dread arriving ahead of proof.

chapters.title: Corvus Knows
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Her handler confronts her with surveillance photos of the bridge and offers a deal: drop Vane, take the bridge assignment officially. She accepts, lying about the phone. Beat: the first real betrayal — of Vane, or of herself, she can't yet say.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Xanthe and Odile Ferrant, a summit security auditor who flagged the same crew and was told to stand down. Their paths cross in an archive basement. Beat: wary alliance; two women who trust documents more than people.

chapters.title: What Vane Buried
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following Vane's clues to a storage unit, she finds his 'death' was staged by the Office itself — and a partial dossier on Operation LULLABY, the plan to let the bridge fall. Beat: the ground tilts; the enemy wears her own badge.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Corvus promotes her onto the summit protection detail — placing her inside the plot's perimeter, and inside its trap. A colleague who asked similar questions has been reassigned to nowhere. Beat: gilded cage; ambition and survival braided together.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She reconstructs the inspection fraud through procurement records and realizes the sabotage timeline ends the morning of the summit. Someone tries to run her car off a coastal road. Beat: fear converted into stubbornness.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Vane arranges a face-to-face in a fish market; he reveals he leaked LULLABY to her because the Office watches everyone else closer than they watch a grieving protégée. He refuses to name the order's author. Beat: reunion shadowed by the question — why won't he just tell her?

chapters.title: The Man Who Signs Nothing
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She traces authorization signatures through cutouts to Deputy Director Halvard Renner, the Office's quiet second-in-command. Confronting him obliquely at a reception, she watches him lie beautifully. Beat: power revealed as performance.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Renner's POV shows him activating a mole hunt; Xanthe's shows her feeding Odile copies of the LULLABY pages while burning her own back-trail. Beat: the hunter learning to move like prey.

chapters.title: The Trap Closes
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Corvus arrests her for treason with evidence too neat — planted by Renner — and offers clemency if she delivers Vane. Beat: despair, then clarity: the frame-up proves how frightened Renner is.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. He surrenders himself to save her, negotiating with Corvus while concealing the archive's location. He admits he helped design LULLABY's contingency before defecting from it. Beat: guilt confessed; loyalty redefined as accountability, not obedience.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, escaped custody via Odile's help. They race the countdown: the epoxy cure time, the convoy schedule, the summit arrival. Beat: relentless momentum; every ally costs something.

chapters.title: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Split POV across Xanthe, Odile, and the saboteur team. Xanthe reaches the joint chambers as the convoy crosses; she triggers a controlled closure of the span, stranding traffic but saving lives, while Odile broadcasts a structural alert that forces official evacuation. Beat: climax — victory purchased with exposure.

chapters.title: Renner's Fall
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. With the attack public, Renner moves to erase LULLABY; Xanthe preempts him using the dead-drop archive, releasing authenticated orders to three governments simultaneously — justice outside any court. Renner is disavowed by his own masters. Beat: cold triumph without satisfaction.

chapters.title: Corvus's Choice
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Ordered to clean house, he instead lets Xanthe and Vane slip the net, keeping a copy of everything as private insurance. Beat: the institutional man discovering self-interest looks remarkably like conscience.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She meets Vane one last time; he declines to run with her, choosing to testify to a foreign tribunal and accept whatever comes. She cannot forgive the design, only understand the repentance. Beat: love and truth finally separated.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The Office formally erases her — passports void, history rewritten. Odile offers her a role with an independent oversight body. Beat: loss transmuted into freedom; identity stripped to its honest core.

chapters.title: The Ringing Stops
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Months later, a new burner arrives in the mail. She holds it over a waste bin, weighs the life she buried against the one she's building, and lets it ring unanswered until it dies. Beat: quiet resolution; the past acknowledged, not obeyed.

chapters.title: Debt and Cover
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Xanthe's POV. At the tribunal where Vane testifies, she sits in the public gallery, unnamed. Justice happens slowly, in daylight, without her hand on it — and she finds she can live with that. Closing beat: the debt paid in truth, the cover surrendered for good.
